stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: Rains shut Chhattisgarh schools; 13 MP districts on heavy rain alert
stories.summary: Heavy rain has shut schools across Chhattisgarh and put riverside villages on flood alert, while the IMD has warned of very heavy rain in 13 Madhya Pradesh districts.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: - Chhattisgarh has closed all government, private and aided schools on Saturday amid heavy rain and flooding concerns.
- Water releases from the Gangrel Dam have raised the alert for villages along the Mahanadi.
- The IMD has warned of very heavy rain in 13 Madhya Pradesh districts as a depression moves towards Uttar Pradesh.
Heavy rain has disrupted travel across parts of Chhattisgarh, prompting a statewide school holiday on Saturday and flood alerts for riverside villages.
In neighbouring Madhya Pradesh, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned of very heavy rain in 13 districts.
Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai ordered all government, private and aided schools to remain closed on 26 September.
He urged parents to keep children at home and directed district administrations to stay ready for relief and rescue work.
Rain has submerged roads and affected connections between districts, particularly in Bastar and adjoining areas.
In Mahasamund, rising water in the Mahanadi and releases from the Gangrel Dam have put 18 riverside villages on alert.
Two guards stranded by floodwater at a liquor shop in Bamhani village were rescued.
All 14 gates of the Gangrel Dam in Dhamtari have been opened as the reservoir filled following sustained rain.
The additional discharge has increased concern for settlements downstream.

stories.headline: Election Commission must respond to SIR irregularity allegations, says Ram Madhav
stories.title: Election Commission must respond to SIR irregularity allegations, says Ram Madhav
stories.summary: BJP leader says Opposition should not contest elections if it believes the electoral system is rigged
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national vice-president V. Ram Madhav said on Friday that the Election Commission of India (ECI) would have to respond to allegations of large-scale irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
He also indicated that Narendra Modi would remain the BJP’s prime ministerial candidate, saying that Mr. Modi would win two or three more elections.

Addressing a memorial lecture, ‘Ism Nee Payanam Etu’, after releasing the book Jaateeya Bhavam Karuvaina Communistlu here, Mr. Ram Madhav said the Congress and other Opposition parties should decide whether their victories in Kerala, Karnataka and Telangana were achieved because of “crumbs” from the BJP.
He said the Opposition should not contest elections if it genuinely believed that the electoral system was rigged.
In an apparent reference to Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Abhijit Dipke and others, Mr. Ram Madhav said some young leaders were emerging but lacked political maturity.

He said they were advising Opposition parties to stay away from what they described as “fixed matches” and “rigged elections”, while claiming that the Opposition had secured small, isolated victories with the BJP’s support.
“Is it so?” he asked the Opposition parties.
Mr. Ram Madhav also criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and questioned how he had concluded that the ECI was helping the BJP win elections.
If that were the case, he said, the ECI constituted by the Congress before 2014 was in place when elections were held in 2014, 2015 and 2016.

Responding to criticism of Mr. Modi’s electoral victories, he said that if the Prime Minister had won three elections without popular support, it was pertinent to recall that Jawaharlal Nehru had also won three elections.
Mr. Modi would win more elections because of his commitment and dedication to uplifting the last person in society, or Antyodaya, he said.

Mr. Ram Madhav said the concept of Antyodaya, articulated by Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya to ensure that the benefits of development reached the last person in society, was reflected in the welfare programmes of the Narendra Modi government.

stories.headline: Plea in Delhi HC seeks 24×7 helpline, safety audits for student PGs after Satya Niketan building collapse
stories.title: Plea in Delhi HC seeks 24×7 helpline, safety audits for student PGs after Satya Niketan building collapse
stories.summary: New Delhi: A fresh Public Interest Litigation has been filed before the Delhi High Court seeking a dedicated mechanism to monitor the safety and welfare of students living in paying guest (PG) accommodations, rented flats and private hostels in Delhi, with the September 6 Satya Niketan building collapse, which claimed seven lives including five students, […] The post Plea in Delhi HC seeks 24×7 helpline, safety audits for student PGs after Satya Niketan building collapse appeared first on KalingaTV .

article_sentences: Plea in Delhi HC seeks 24x7 helpline and mandatory safety audits for student PGs following the Satya Niketan building collapse.

New Delhi: A fresh Public Interest Litigation has been filed before the Delhi High Court seeking a dedicated mechanism to monitor the safety and welfare of students living in paying guest (PG) accommodations, rented flats and private hostels in Delhi, with the September 6 Satya Niketan building collapse, which claimed seven lives including five students, cited as the immediate trigger for the plea.

The petition has been filed by Shivansh Kalia, a second-year student of PGDAV College, University of Delhi, who has sought constitution of Student Accommodation Advisory and Monitoring Committees at college, university and major student/coaching-hub levels.
The plea has been filed through advocate Ashu Bidhuri.
The PIL comes against the backdrop of the Satya Niketan tragedy, where a building being used as a private boys’ hostel/PG accommodation collapsed on September 6.
The petition states that seven persons, including five students, died in the incident and several others were rescued from the debris.
It further refers to reports raising questions over construction and renovation work carried out shortly before the collapse and the sanctioned structure of the building.

The Delhi High Court had, while dealing with proceedings arising from the Satya Niketan collapse, observed on September 7 that responsibility for such mishaps, prima facie, does not lie solely with the PG owner and also extends to university authorities and the MCD, which is responsible for ensuring compliance with building bye-laws and regulations.

The latest PIL seeks to build on that concern by creating a coordinated institutional mechanism for students who are dependent on private accommodation because of the limited availability of institutional hostels.

The plea says existing responsibilities are distributed among the MCD, Delhi Fire Services, Police, district administration and educational institutions, but students do not have a single dedicated mechanism to report accommodation-related safety concerns and seek coordinated intervention.

The petitioner has proposed that the committees have a 24×7 student helpline, dedicated email address and online grievance portal through which students could report structural and fire hazards, overcrowding, electrical and sanitation problems, exploitation, harassment and other accommodation-related grievances.

The proposed committees would also facilitate periodic safety verification of student accommodations, coordinate structural, electrical and fire-safety assessments with competent authorities, identify unsafe or unauthorised premises and refer them to the relevant statutory authorities for action.

stories.summary: A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Viswanathan also formed a judicial commission, led by former Supreme Court judge Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia, to conduct a thorough inquiry in Uldepur, on the outskirts of Meerut, regarding the nature of land where these illegal residential colonies have developed

article_sentences: Taking serious note of illegal constructions and the conversion of residential properties for commercial use, the Supreme Court has directed the Uttar Pradesh government to seal over 16,000 properties in Meerut and demolish unauthorised structures.

A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Viswanathan also formed a judicial commission, led by former Supreme Court judge Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia, to conduct a thorough inquiry in Uldepur, on the outskirts of Meerut, regarding the nature of land where these illegal residential colonies have developed.

"We are shocked and disturbed to learn, reading the status report, that hundreds of illegal residential colonies have come up at Uldepur," the Bench said, after perusing the report by P. Guruprasad, Chairman of Uttar Pradesh Awas Evam Vikas Parishad.
The Bench noted that the department has undertaken an inspection and survey of various parts of Meerut.
The report showed that the town has been divided into four zones: Zone-A, Zone-B, Zone-C, and Zone-D.
"In Zone-A, 16 teams deputed for the purpose of inspection/survey have identified 16,726 structures to be absolutely illegal/unauthorised.
Out of 16,726 structures, 12,907 comprise residential, 874 residential-cum-non- residential, and 2945 non-residential constructions," it noted in its September 21 order.

The top court, hearing a contempt petition related to non-compliance with previous directives on illegal constructions, instructed the authorities to take appropriate action against all the 16,726 illegal structures in Zone-A at the earliest.
"The first step in the process is to ask the occupants to vacate the premises and to seal all these premises, i.e., the 16,726 illegal structures.
We direct accordingly.
It is possible that some of these structures may be in a dilapidated condition and may collapse, resulting in casualties.
We do not want this to happen at any cost.

stories.title: Maharashtra declares 265 of 358 talukas drought-hit, announces relief
stories.summary: The Maharashtra government on Saturday declared 265 of the 358 talukas in the state as drought-affected, announcing relief measures, including restructuring of crop loans, concession in land revenue and deferment of recovery of agriculture-related loans. According to a government resolution issued late on Friday, this covers 74 per cent of the state. The decision follows Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis's recent visit to some drought-affected parts of the state. The state government has activated 'Trigger-1' under its manual for drought management 2016 (updated in 2020) and Drought Management Code to declare drought conditions and initiate relief. Trigger-1 is the first stage in the state's drought framework, activated by a rainfall deficit of more than 25 per cent combined with a prolonged dry spell of 21 days. stories.headline: Substance abuse among children is a child protection issue: CJI Surya Kant
stories.title: Substance abuse among children is a child protection issue: CJI Surya Kant
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Saturday said substance abuse among children must be understood as a child protection issue, rather than as a matter of public health concern. Delivering the Pataliputra Pragya Pravah lecture on 'Childhood Beyond Drugs: Protection, Care and Reintegration' at the Bihar Lok Bhavan here, Justice Kant cited a recent Lancet study to say that at least one in five teenagers in India were at moderate to high risk of substance abuse. "Substance abuse among children must be understood not only as a matter of public health concern, but as a child protection issue as well," he said. Justice Kant stressed the need for a "child-sensitive response" to addiction to protect not only the child's physical and mental well-being but also their dignity and sense of self-worth. stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses BJP MLAs' Plea Challenging Quashing Of Corruption Complaint Against Karnataka Energy Minister KJ George
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (25 September) dismissed a Special Leave Petition (SLP) against the Karnataka High Court's judgment which had quashed criminal complaint against Karnataka's Energy Minister KJ George and Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM) officials over alleged irregularities in the tender procurement and installation of smart electricity meters in Karnataka.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran declined to interfere with the High Court's order, holding that there existed “no good ground to interfere with the impugned order passed by the High Court.”

A criminal complaint was filed against Minister KJ George and BESCOM officials, by three MLAs (CN Ashwath Narayan, SR Vishwanath, and Dheeraj Muniraj) of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), alleging offences under Sections 314, 316, and 61 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), and Section 13(1)(a), 13(1)(b) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (PC Act), in connection with the tender for smart meters.
The MLAs had first approached the Lokayukta police before filing the complaint before the PC Act Special Court.

On George's petition seeking quashing of the proceedings, the Karnataka High Court had quashed the proceedings reasoning that it had found no material to substantiate the corruption allegation, and no allegation of any pecuniary benefit having been received by the Minister.
Aggrieved by the High Court's ruling, the BJP MLAs filed an SLP before the Supreme Court.
“Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and having gone through the materials on record, we find no good ground to interfere with the impugned order passed by the High Court.”
For Petitioners: Mr. Lakshmy Iyenger, Sr. Adv.; Mr. Dhawesh Pahuja, AOR; Mr. Saket Gogia, Adv.; Mr. Aakash Vt, Adv.; Mr. Harshith S, Adv.; Ms. Gauri Pande, Adv.; Mr. Mansingh, Adv.
Mr. Deepesh Meena, Adv.; Mr. Adithya KS, Adv.; Ms. Harshita Singh Tomar, Adv.
For Respondents: Mr. Kapil Sibal, Sr. Adv.; Mr. Vivek Jain, AOR; Ms. Suchitra Kumbhat, Adv.
Mr. Rohit H Nair, Adv.; Ms. Ishika Gandhi, Adv.; Mr. Shathabish Shivanna, Adv.; Mr. Abhishek Janardhan, Adv.; Mr. Samrudh Suraj Hegde, Adv.
